text:
Maya S: heads up, noticed customer hit duplicate side-effects from streaming completions after a 429 flood during a region failover.
Hugo P: high level: SDK retried entire streaming POST and caused a second downstream webhook call?
Maya S: exactly. they stream incremental events; after the first chunk the server triggers an external webhook. connection drops, SDK retries, webhook gets called again.
Lin Z: rough numbers? how often are retries happening?
Maya S: saw a spike: ~1200 retries in 10 minutes, most were fast retries (no jitter) because client backoff is linear by default.
CI-Bot: flakiness test triggered: examples/streaming-idempotency/test_flaky_retry failing on master #4821
Nora K: linear backoff + no jitter is a classic amplifier for thundering replays. We should force randomized jitter for streaming endpoints at least.
Owen R: aggree. also streaming endpoints need a different retry policy: default should be "no auto-replay" unless server advertises resume or client sets safe flag.
Hugo P: proposal: 1) SDK default: never auto-retry streaming POSTs. 2) If server sends header `x-rw-resume-window` with a token, allow resume-based retry where client attaches `x-rw-resume-token`. 3) If user explicitly sets `allow_unsafe_replay=true`, apply standard retry policy with strong jitter and exponential backoff.
Maya S: that matches my instincts. can we make the SDK warn loudly in logs when unsafe replay would have happened?
Lin Z: yes, emit `sdk.warn.replay_blocked` with context hash (not prompt) so we can triage without PII.
Nora K: about jitter: recommend full jitter per AWS blog: sleep = random(0, base * 2^attempt). We'll set base=250ms and cap at 10s for streaming unsafe mode.
Owen R: also add a small token-based local replay guard so clients without server resume support can still avoid a quick duplicate: store ephemeral fingerprint of first-chunk event ids and refrain from immediate retry for 30s. Not perfect but reduces dupes.
Hugo P: fingerprinting rules: hash(event ids + path + client-salt). Must not persist to disk and must be opt-out for privacy.
Maya S: sample app idea: examples/streaming-replay-policy with toggles: RESUME_SUPPORT=1, ALLOW_UNSAFE=1, CLIENT_SALT=env. We can show 3 modes and webhook counts.
CI-Bot: test plan: add an e2e that simulates drop-after=N and asserts webhook calls==1 when RESUME_SUPPORT=1, and ==2 when ALLOW_UNSAFE=1.
Lin Z: server work: add `x-rw-resume-window` header on first flush and accept `x-rw-resume-token` on retry. RFC needed for token format and expiration semantics.
Nora K: docs: update SDK retry page and call out "Streaming semantics: idempotency_key does not imply streaming safety" with code snippets for Node/Python/Go.
Owen R: telemetry: counters `sdk.streaming.retry_attempts`, `sdk.streaming.resume_used`, `sdk.streaming.replay_blocked`. Make those taggable by sdk_language.
Maya S: security note: do not include prompt text in logs or hashed keys. Always salt with ephemeral per-process value.
Hugo P: can we fallback to server-side dedupe? e.g., server can emit `x-rw-event-id` per chunk and third-party webhook can use it if they support idempotency. But customer said webhook is external and immutable for now, so we need client-side mitigation.
Lin Z: timeline: I'll draft server RFC this week. Hugo and Owen can PR SDK changes next sprint. Maya will craft sample app and notebook. Nora will update docs.
Maya S: thanks. quick action: I'll open GH issue linking logs and sample repro and tag eng-oncall and security.
Hugo P: thumbs up. small follow-up: enforce jitter in core SDK backoff util so all languages pick it up.
CI-Bot: created issue #6013: streaming-replay-safe-default and linked PR template.
Maya S: tagging folks to review: @HugoP @LinZ @NoraK. if anyone wants to try the sample, ping me for access to the repro harness.
Owen R: great, this should stop accidental duplicates in many cases.
Maya S: end of thread.
